correctness.rationale: All quantifiers include arbitrary finite n and both positive conditioning probabilities. For positive triples the product quadratic is strictly Hurwitz stable, the classical even/odd Hermite--Biehler theorem gives alternating Bernoulli parameters, and the variance difference is the exact integral of (1-2x) times an indicator-valued interlacing count. Its positive and negative areas equal 1/4. Perturbation handles boundary triples; explicit one- and two-summand examples attain both endpoints. 53,886 exact rational finite-law tests corroborate, but do not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The intrinsic dispersion of an integer-versus-half-integer total score is a natural uncertainty quantity for independent win/tie/loss competition scores and ternary reliability outcomes. Individual conditional variances can scale with n, but their discrepancy has a sharp dimension-free 1/4 bound of either sign, giving a nontrivial calibration unavailable from known mean/mode or fixed-distance coupling inequalities. Explicit extremizers show neither constant can be improved.
